input: Make a scrapbook of last summer's road trip

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing which destinations, days, or moments to include shapes how much material needs to be gathered and how the scrapbook is structured.
Whether this is a personal keepsake, a gift for a travel companion, or something to share with family changes the tone, content emphasis, and level of personalisation.
A physical scrapbook requires craft supplies and assembly time, while a digital one requires software and different skills — this is a foundational format decision.
A deadline (e.g. a birthday or holiday gift) or a budget for materials directly affects how ambitious the project can be and how to prioritise effort.
Understanding what raw materials already exist — photos printed vs. on a phone, ticket stubs, maps — determines what needs to be gathered or ordered before starting.
Style choices (minimalist vs. eclectic, heavily journaled vs. photo-forward) define what supplies to buy and how much time to budget per page.
Knowing what 'done well' looks like — a polished gift-quality album vs. a casual personal memory book — sets the quality bar and prevents over- or under-investing effort.

gold.taskTitle: Make a scrapbook of last summer's road trip
gold.taskDescription: Create a scrapbook capturing memories from last summer's road trip, in a format and style yet to be determined.

questions.title: Which stops or moments must be included?
questions.description: Identify whether the scrapbook covers the entire trip chronologically, highlights specific destinations, or focuses on standout moments only.

questions.title: Who is this scrapbook being made for?
questions.description: Clarify if this is a personal keepsake, a gift for a fellow traveller, or something to share with family — this shapes tone and content.

questions.title: Should this be a physical or digital scrapbook?
questions.description: Determine the medium — handmade physical album, a printed photo book service, or a digital format — as this drives every downstream decision about tools and materials.

questions.title: Is there a deadline this needs to be finished by?
questions.description: Establish whether there is a fixed date (e.g. a gift occasion or reunion) that sets the pace and scope of the project.

questions.title: What materials do you already have on hand?
questions.description: Inventory existing assets — printed photos, digital photos, physical mementos like tickets or maps — to determine what still needs to be gathered or ordered.

questions.title: What visual style are you going for?
questions.description: Establish aesthetic preferences such as minimalist and clean, colourful and eclectic, heavily journaled with captions, or mostly photo-forward.

questions.title: What does a finished, successful scrapbook look like to you?
questions.description: Define the quality bar — a polished, gift-ready album vs. a casual personal memory book — to calibrate how much time and detail to invest.
